title: sharded-ringbuffer-and-zero-copy-pipeline-to-reduce-host-handoff-overhead
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Host-side overhead during prefill->decode handoff creates CPU saturation, extra memcpy costs, and threadpool lock contention for high-concurrency workloads. This manifests as elevated p99 latency and higher per-token CPU footprint for hosted endpoints.

Goal: Reduce CPU-to-GPU handoff overhead and threadpool contention by introducing a sharded, lock-minimized host-to-device pipeline that uses pinned/zero-copy regions where safe, and adaptive batching/coalescing for small prefill requests. Target metrics: reduce host CPU utilization for steady-state text gen by 40% and improve tokens/sec by >=25% for mixed short/long workloads without regressing model quality or tail latency.

Design proposal (summary):
- Sharded ring-buffers per NUMA socket / worker group to avoid a single global queue and lock hot path. Each shard is implemented as an SPSC or MPMC ring depending on producer/consumer ratio and uses cache-aligned head/tail pointers to avoid false sharing.
- Pinned host buffers (cudaHostAlloc / MAP_POPULATE pattern) for prefill KV pages to enable async DMA to GPU and avoid an extra CPU memcpy on the hot path. Use explicit fallbacks for environments where pinned allocation is unavailable.
- Zero-copy mapped windows for small-frag requests: for small prefill payloads we map a short-lived window that the GPU kernel can read directly, avoiding a staging memcpy.
- Replace coarse global threadpool locks with a light-weight work-stealing pool per shard. Use lock-free task handoff where possible and a bounded executor for decode tasks to ensure latency SLOs.
- Adaptive coalescing: short-lived prefill requests arriving within a tunable window (e.g., 250us) are coalesced into a single GPU batch to amortize kernel launch overhead. A short-window admission controller prevents excessive queuing.
- Kernel-selection hints: pass sequence-length distribution metadata from the host pipeline to the scheduler so the runtime can prefer fused/faster attention kernels for short sequences and different kernels for long sequences. This reduces kernel-switching overhead and improves occupancy.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Pinned allocations increase host memory pressure; must cap total pinned footprint per host and evict least-recently-used pinned pages.
- Zero-copy mapping depends on kernel/driver support; older drivers may require fallback to memcpy path which increases code complexity.
- Work-stealing per shard may increase code paths and subtle concurrency bugs; additional test coverage is required.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end synthetic perf shows >=30% reduction in steady-state host CPU for 8xA100 cluster mix and tokens/sec >=1.25x baseline for mixed workload.
- p99 total latency not worse than baseline +5%.
- Feature gated behind runtime flag and safe fallback to existing pipeline.

Artifacts and references: design doc, perf dashboard, initial PoC PRs are linked below.
comments: 2025-06-12 Maya Patel: Created ticket after perf spikes observed in hosted q3 benchmark. Initial triage indicates most cycles spent in memcpy + global queue lock during prefill handling.

2025-06-14 Javier Ortega: POC implemented: sharded ring buffer + pinned host buffer allocation. Microbenchmarks show memcpy removed for 90% of small prefill cases and host CPU down ~28% in single-host test. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7284

2025-06-18 Lina Huang: Review feedback: add robust fallback when cudaHostAlloc fails and add caps to pinned memory. Also asked for NUMA-aware placement tests on c6i-like instances for CPU-heavy workloads.

2025-06-20 Perf run: 50k-req mixed-shot workload across 4 hosts. Results: host CPU median reduced from 42%->18%, tokens/sec +35%, p50 latency -12%, p99 latency -6%. Raw dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboards/ENG-15643

2025-06-22 QA: Found intermittent CI failure on driver matrix (NVIDIA driver 470.x) where zero-copy mapping triggers segmentation fault. Marking as blocked on infra:ENG to curate driver fallback. Added task ENG-15644 to track driver shims.

2025-06-24 Javier Ortega: Addressed lock-free queue edge-case and added stress tests for work-stealing pool. Prepared canary rollout plan (10% traffic, runtime flag). PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7339

2025-06-25 Maya Patel: Next steps: unblock driver fallback (ENG-15644), add observability metrics for pinned footprint and per-shard queue depth, and schedule canary for runtime-1.21-alpha. Also create a follow-up ticket to propagate kernel-selection hints into the model catalog for per-model defaults (PM-4127).
